prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1153; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not say my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?
A: I was driving on a main road in Sugar Land, heading toward the shopping center. It was pretty slow traffic.
Q: What was the weather and road condition like?
A: It was clear, and the pavement was dry. Nothing unusual.
Q: Walk me through what happened right before the impact.
A: The car in front of me stopped suddenly, so I braked. The other vehicle came over the center line and hit me head-on, but it wasn't going very fast. I'd guess it was maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour.
Q: Did you have any time to react?
A: Not really. I got the brakes on, but there wasn't time to steer away.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: How are you feeling physically since the collision?
A: My lower back is sore and tight. I've been stiff when I get up in the morning, and it hurts to sit for long periods.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment?
A: I went to urgent care that same day. They gave me muscle relaxers and told me to follow up with my regular physician.
Q: Did you have any back problems before this accident?
A: I had some occasional soreness from lifting at work, but nothing that kept me from my normal activities.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I appreciate you following up.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
